## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
=====
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
  `package-lock.json`s, and `vendor/wasm_run/native/Cargo.lock`); a listed
  lockfile that is missing/untracked/gitignored fails the Static gates, and
  pod-sync (flutter-analyze + nightly build legs, after `pub get`) fails
  when a native iOS/macOS plugin resolved by pubspec.lock has no pod in the
  platform's `Podfile.lock` (the gh-1274 class), or its pod is pinned at a
  stale version vs the resolved plugin podspec's `s.version` (the
  flutter_gemma 1.8.0-vs-1.11.3 skew; the podspec is the comparison target,
  not the pubspec version — vendored/beta pods legitimately differ from the
  Dart package version). After ANY pubspec.yaml
  dependency change that adds/updates a darwin-native plugin: `cd
  flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update` and the same in `macos/`,
  commit both `Podfile.lock`s (CocoaPods runs fine on Linux for
  regeneration; the wasm_run `nm` step needs an llvm-nm shim + the
  XCFramework staged via `scripts/setup_vendor_ios.sh` or the upstream zip).
  Guard red exits are fixture-self-tested (`scripts/
  check_lockfiles_selftest.sh`, Static gates).
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the le…

### Correctness of `balancedJsonObjectAfter`

Let me trace through edge cases:

1. **Escape handling inside strings**: `\"` correctly skipped via `i++`. `\\` also. An escape at the very end (`i++` past length) → loop exits, returns null (unbalanced) — correct.

2. **Single quotes**: JSON strings are always double-quoted (JSON.stringify). But the ENVELOPE (`{id: [E] faAppError:...}`) is not JSON. The scan starts at the record's `{`, so envelope content doesn't matter. OK.

3. **The scan starts at the first `{` AFTER the marker** — so if a plain log line mentions the marker followed by text without `{`, returns null. If a log line contains `faAppError: {some other json}` that jsonDecodes to a Map with `message` — a false positive could capture a plain log as an error. That was equally possible in the old code (old code would also decode `{some other json}` if it were valid JSON with message field). No regression.

4. **Multiple `}` inside the record's strings** — handled by string-awareness.

5. **What if the record is valid but the envelope `}` trails** — handled (scan returns at record's balanced close).

6. **Behavior change for old wire shape**: `[E] faAppError:{json}` → old: substring to end = `{json}` → decode. New: balanced scan → `{json}`. Same. ✅ Backward compatible.

7. **Whitespace after marker**: old code `.trim()`ed the payload. New: `balancedJsonObjectAfter(line, index + marker.length)` — `indexOf('{', from)` skips leading whitespace. Equivalent. Trailing whitespace after record: old decode of `{json}  `.trim() would still work; new returns `{json}` — same. ✅

8. **Surrogate pairs**: no issue.

9. **`line[i]` performance**: For log lines this is O(n) — fine.

Now a REAL edge case worth thinking about: **a JSON string containing a backslash at end of string in the ENVELOPE** — not applicable since scan starts at record.

**A record that itself is not at the first `{` after marker**: e.g. line = `[E] faAppError: see {docs} then {"kind":"showError","message":"x"}`. New code picks `{docs}` → not balanced JSON (well `{docs}` IS balanced) → decode fails → null → capture misses. Old code: `see {docs} then {...}` → decode fails → null too. Same behavior (both miss). Not a regression, and not a real wire shape.

---
  flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:

Now I have a complete picture of the CI gating:

- PR gate (`ci.yml` `flutter-tests`, ubuntu-24.04-arm): runs all non-golden tests but with `--exclude-tags integration`, and the native-dependent tests are "NOT excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in `flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart`". So `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` runs on the PR gate but is SKIPPED via `quickJsBridgeAvailable ? false : kQuickJsBridgeUnavailable` guard — on ubuntu-arm without the native QuickJS bridge, `_engineSkip` is true and the group is skipped. That's the exclusion-zone hole: the capture test needs the native QuickJS bridge (available on macOS nightly), skipped on the PR gate.

Wait — actually the comment says quickjs_c_bridge .so tests are host-portable via the skip guard — meaning they RUN where the bridge is available, skip otherwise. On ubuntu-arm CI, presumably no quickjs .so → skipped. So yes: the PR gate cannot catch this class; the nightly macOS leg can. This is exactly NG1/#1267 N1 — out of scope for this PR (fixing the parser), and the ticket itself cross-references it as a separate card (#1267).

Note the ticket's AC1: "nightly flutter_app suite (macOS) green again; the capture test passes on main" — can only be verified post-merge on the next nightly. The PR description claims local verification with the native bridge (528 passed). I can't re-run that here (linux, no quickjs bridge). The pure-Dart parser tests I ran do pass.

Now — is there a change ci.yml leg that runs the parser test? The parser test (`js_app_error_channel_test.dart`) is pure Dart, runs on ubuntu gate. Good — the NEW tests added in this PR DO run in the PR gate. That's the key improvement: the regression surface (parser) now has gate-visible coverage (NG2 spirit: the pure parser tests run everywhere).

Now the exhaustive code review of the diff itself:

### `balancedJsonObjectAfter` — deeper edge cases

1. `i++; // skip the escaped character verbatim` — when the backslash is the final char, `i` becomes `line.length` → loop ends → null. OK.

2. **String-awareness starts at the record's `{`** — good; but what if the record itself is preceded (after marker) by garbage containing `"`? e.g. `faAppError: "unterminated` then record. Hypothetical; not a wire shape.

3. What about a line where the marker appears INSIDE a JSON string before the real record? e.g. a console.log line `faAppError: is handled by {"kind":...}` — old code: substring from marker to end = ` is handled by {...}` → decode fail → null. New code: first `{` after marker → `{"kind":...}` — if that JSON has non-empty `message`, it would NOW be captured where old code returned null! False-positive class: a plain log line that mentions `faAppError:` followed later by arbitrary valid JSON with a message field. How real is this? The bootstrap is the only thing that emits `faAppError:` (marker doc says "Never remove or reword the marker"). A widget's own console.log could mention the marker in passing — plausible in theory ("don't use faAppError: yourself"), followed by an unrelated JSON dump. Risk is LOW (requires marker mention + subsequent valid JSON with message), and the failure mode is a spurious error report passing the dedup gate — annoying, not breaking. It's a SUGGESTION-level observation: the parser is now a heuristic; could tighten by requiring the balanced object to IMMEDIATELY follow the marker modulo whitespace (`^\s*\{`). Actually wait — would requiring immediate-`{` break the actual envelope shape? Envelope: `{id: [E] faAppError:{...}}` — record `{` immediately follows the marker (no space). And plain record `[E] faAppError:{json}` — also immediate. The old code `.trim()`ed, implying whitespace was tolerated. Requiring the first non-space char after marker to be `{` would preserve both observed shapes AND kill the false-positive class. But then a hypothetical envelope like `faAppError: prefix {...}` would be missed — no observed shape needs that. This is a legitimate hardening suggestion — SUGGESTION level since no observed wire shape puts junk between marker and record.

Hmm, but is it important enough? The tradeoff: tolerance (current) vs precision. The doc comment explicitly says "a marker mention inside a plain log line still returns null" — that claim is only true when no balanced JSON object with a `message` follows the mention. Slightly overstated doc. I'll file as SUGGESTION.

4. **`@visibleForTesting` on `balancedJsonObjectAfter`** — the function IS called from production code (`parseJsAppErrorLogLine`, same library). `visibleForTesting` means "do not reference from production code OUTSIDE this library"; in-library use is legal, no analyzer error (I verified: analyzer clean). But the annotation is semantically wrong — it tells readers/tools this is test-only surface, when it's actually a production helper that is additionally exported for tests. The file's own convention: `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` is public, no annotation, doc says "Exported for the engine's log tap and for tests". Consistent fix: drop the annotation (or keep the function private and test through parseJsAppErrorLogLine). Actually — testing `balancedJsonObjectAfter` directly isn't even done in the tests! The new tests only exercise `parseJsAppErrorLogLine`. So the annotation is doubly odd: it's not used by any test directly. Making it private (`_balancedJsonObjectAfter`) would be cleaner — no public API growth. SUGGESTION (API surface minimization). Actually, since it's used only within the library, private is strictly better: smaller public surface on a lib that `flutter_app` exports via `package:fa/apps/...`. ## PR Description

Closes #1307
## Root Cause

- The gh-1164 error-capture surface was blind: `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` required the `faAppError:{json}` record to run to end-of-line, but by the time an engine log line reaches Dart it is wrapped in the runtime's iid-transport envelope — `{id: [E] faAppError:{…}}` (flutter_js `jsonDecode`s the `sendMessage` payload before the channel callback, so the bootstrap's `{"iid":…,"id":…}` wrap survives routing). The envelope's trailing brace made the payload malformed JSON → decode failed → `null` → the capture list stayed empty.
- #1273 (gh-1272) didn't break this path — it un-blinded it: before the raw-string bootstrap fix, no `faAppError` record was ever emitted (every widget dead); once records flowed again, the downstream parser mismatch surfaced. Green PR because the macOS flutter_app suite sits in the PR exclusion zone (#1267 N1 scenario, cross-linked).

## Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_error_channel.dart`: `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` now decodes the first **balanced** `{…}` object after the `faAppError:` marker (string-literal/escape-aware scan) instead of the exact rest-of-line — any transport envelope around the record decodes; plain-log marker mentions still return `null`. No change to the wire format, the bootstrap, #1272's raw-string fix, or the pinned `js_widget_runtime` package.

## Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_error_channel_test.dart`: 4 new pure-Dart parser tests (plain record, iid-enveloped record, nested braces/escapes, negative cases) — run everywhere, no JS bridge needed.
- `test/apps/js_app_error_capture_test.dart` (the red nightly suite): 3/3 PASSED with the native QuickJS bridge.
- Full `flutter_app/test/apps/` with the bridge: **528 passed, 0 failed** (incl. the gh-1272 regex round-trip group — AC2: corrupted/regex-heavy sources still eval, and load throws are captured with a readable `Widget error: …` message); engine suite 68 passed; agent_service error-delivery suite passed. Analyzer clean on touched files.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
=====
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP

Now let me do the deep review of the actual change. Key analysis points so far:

### Correctness of `balancedJsonObjectAfter`

Let me trace through edge cases:

1. **Escape handling inside strings**: `\"` correctly skipped via `i++`. `\\` also. An escape at the very end (`i++` past length) → loop exits, returns null (unbalanced) — correct.

2. **Single quotes**: JSON strings are always double-quoted (JSON.stringify). But the ENVELOPE (`{id: [E] faAppError:...}`) is not JSON. The scan starts at the record's `{`, so envelope content doesn't matter. OK.

3. **The scan starts at the first `{` AFTER the marker** — so if a plain log line mentions the marker followed by text without `{`, returns null. If a log line contains `faAppError: {some other json}` that jsonDecodes to a Map with `message` — a false positive could capture a plain log as an error. That was equally possible in the old code (old code would also decode `{some other json}` if it were valid JSON with message field). No regression.

4. **Multiple `}` inside the record's strings** — handled by string-awareness.

5. **What if the record is valid but the envelope `}` trails** — handled (scan returns at record's balanced close).

6. **Behavior change for old wire shape**: `[E] faAppError:{json}` → old: substring to end = `{json}` → decode. New: balanced scan → `{json}`. Same. ✅ Backward compatible.

7. **Whitespace after marker**: old code `.trim()`ed the payload. New: `balancedJsonObjectAfter(line, index + marker.length)` — `indexOf('{', from)` skips leading whitespace. Equivalent. Trailing whitespace after record: old decode of `{json}  `.trim() would still work; new returns `{json}` — same. ✅

8. **Surrogate pairs**: no issue.

9. **`line[i]` performance**: For log lines this is O(n) — fine.

Now a REAL edge case worth thinking about: **a JSON string containing a backslash at end of string in the ENVELOPE** — not applicable since scan starts at record.

**A record that itself is not at the first `{` after marker**: e.g. line = `[E] faAppError: see {docs} then {"kind":"showError","message":"x"}`. New code picks `{docs}` → not balanced JSON (well `{docs}` IS balanced) → decode fails → null → capture misses. Old code: `see {docs} then {...}` → decode fails → null too. Same behavior (both miss). Not a regression, and not a real wire shape.

**The critical scenario the ticket cares about**: does the actual transport line contain the marker with the record AFTER it as the first `{`? Observed shape per PR/tests: `{id: [E] faAppError:{…}}` — yes, record's `{` is the first `{` after the marker. ✅

### Now the deeper question — NG2: "ONE canonical error surface"

The ticket's NG2 asks for one canonical error surface so a fix in one can't blind the other. This PR patches the parser tolerantly, but the ENGINE test (`js_app_error_capture_test.dart`) requires the real QuickJS bridge (skipped without it) — and the macOS suite is in the PR exclusion zone (the whole reason this regressed).   flutter-tests:
    name: Flutter app tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    # End-of-run drain can stall minutes under shared-runner load while
    # every test already passed (0 failures, killed mid-drain on #330):
    # fa_ui shards get 12m and flutter_app is the heaviest package.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # arm64: no official linux-arm64 release tarball (x64-only manifest) —
      # subosito/flutter-action cannot fetch stable here. Bootstrap via git
      # clone instead: flutter_tools pulls the official arm64 Dart SDK itself.
      - name: Flutter SDK (arm64 git bootstrap)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 -b stable https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git "$HOME/flutter"
          echo "$HOME/flutter/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/flutter/bin:$PATH"
          flutter --version
          flutter precache
      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/pubspec.yaml') }}
          restore-keys: pubcache-flutter-${{ runner.os }}-

      # See flutter-analyze: placeholder must exist before pub get.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile

      # Golden suite is intentionally NOT here: goldens are host-locked
      # (same macOS host renders them differently across minor SDKs — see the
      # dynamic_messages saga) and would all redden on ubuntu. Widget/unit
      # tests run here on a cheap runner; goldens stay guarded by
      # build-macos.yml and the nightly full matrix (issue #177 E5/OQ3:
      # pinned-font golden migration is a follow-up, not this card).
      - name: flutter test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
        # Goldens stay out (host-locked, see the golden comment above).
        # Native-dependent tests (quickjs_c_bridge .so, mic channel) are NOT
        # excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in
        # flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart + the injected-ASR fix.
        # Deterministic modulo split of the sorted file list: shard i takes
        # lines where NR % 2 == i — union == the old single job's list.
        run: |
          cd flutter_app
          find test -name '*_test.dart' ! -path '*/golden/*' ! -path '*/cli_visual/*' \
            | sort | awk -v i=${{ matrix.shard }} 'NR % 2 == i' > shard-files.txt
          echo "shard files: $(wc -l < shard-files.txt)"
          # --coverage (issue #433): each shard emits lcov for the
          # app-crap-gate job; the covered surface matches the CRAP
          # sources [lib] exactly.
          flutter test --exclude-tags integration --coverage $(cat shard-files.txt)

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: app-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2

      # Issue #239 AC3: the App Store submission pre-flight matrix is plain
      # ruby over flutter_app/fastlane/appstore_preflight.rb — no gems,
      # runs in under a second on the runner's stock ruby.
      # Issue #289 adds the fastlane guard/preflight suites (android id
      # guard + Play upload pre-flight) — same plain-ruby contract, so the
      # step loops over every fastlane test file. Shard 0 only: once is
      # enough (fa PR #333).
      - name: Fastlane pre-flight suites (ruby)
        if: matrix.shard == 0
        run: |
          for t in flutter_app/fastlane/test/*_test.rb; do
            echo "::group::ruby $t"
            ruby "$t"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:

Now I have a complete picture of the CI gating:

- PR gate (`ci.yml` `flutter-tests`, ubuntu-24.04-arm): runs all non-golden tests but with `--exclude-tags integration`, and the native-dependent tests are "NOT excluded — issue #184 made them host-portable via the skip guard in `flutter_app/test/native_test_guard.dart`". So `js_app_error_capture_test.dart` runs on the PR gate but is SKIPPED via `quickJsBridgeAvailable ? false : kQuickJsBridgeUnavailable` guard — on ubuntu-arm without the native QuickJS bridge, `_engineSkip` is true and the group is skipped. That's the exclusion-zone hole: the capture test needs the native QuickJS bridge (available on macOS nightly), skipped on the PR gate.

Wait — actually the comment says quickjs_c_bridge .so tests are host-portable via the skip guard — meaning they RUN where the bridge is available, skip otherwise. On ubuntu-arm CI, presumably no quickjs .so → skipped. So yes: the PR gate cannot catch this class; the nightly macOS leg can. This is exactly NG1/#1267 N1 — out of scope for this PR (fixing the parser), and the ticket itself cross-references it as a separate card (#1267).

Note the ticket's AC1: "nightly flutter_app suite (macOS) green again; the capture test passes on main" — can only be verified post-merge on the next nightly. The PR description claims local verification with the native bridge (528 passed). I can't re-run that here (linux, no quickjs bridge). The pure-Dart parser tests I ran do pass.

Now — is there a change ci.yml leg that runs the parser test? The parser test (`js_app_error_channel_test.dart`) is pure Dart, runs on ubuntu gate. Good — the NEW tests added in this PR DO run in the PR gate. That's the key improvement: the regression surface (parser) now has gate-visible coverage (NG2 spirit: the pure parser tests run everywhere).

Now the exhaustive code review of the diff itself:

### `balancedJsonObjectAfter` — deeper edge cases

1. `i++; // skip the escaped character verbatim` — when the backslash is the final char, `i` becomes `line.length` → loop ends → null. OK.

2. **String-awareness starts at the record's `{`** — good; but what if the record itself is preceded (after marker) by garbage containing `"`? e.g. `faAppError: "unterminated` then record. Hypothetical; not a wire shape.

3. What about a line where the marker appears INSIDE a JSON string before the real record? e.g. a console.log line `faAppError: is handled by {"kind":...}` — old code: substring from marker to end = ` is handled by {...}` → decode fail → null. New code: first `{` after marker → `{"kind":...}` — if that JSON has non-empty `message`, it would NOW be captured where old code returned null! False-positive class: a plain log line that mentions `faAppError:` followed later by arbitrary valid JSON with a message field. How real is this? The bootstrap is the only thing that emits `faAppError:` (marker doc says "Never remove or reword the marker"). A widget's own console.log could mention the marker in passing — plausible in theory ("don't use faAppError: yourself"), followed by an unrelated JSON dump. Risk is LOW (requires marker mention + subsequent valid JSON with message), and the failure mode is a spurious error report passing the dedup gate — annoying, not breaking. It's a SUGGESTION-level observation: the parser is now a heuristic; could tighten by requiring the balanced object to IMMEDIATELY follow the marker modulo whitespace (`^\s*\{`). Actually wait — would requiring immediate-`{` break the actual envelope shape? Envelope: `{id: [E] faAppError:{...}}` — record `{` immediately follows the marker (no space). And plain record `[E] faAppError:{json}` — also immediate. The old code `.trim()`ed, implying whitespace was tolerated. Requiring the first non-space char after marker to be `{` would preserve both observed shapes AND kill the false-positive class. But then a hypothetical envelope like `faAppError: prefix {...}` would be missed — no observed shape needs that. This is a legitimate hardening suggestion — SUGGESTION level since no observed wire shape puts junk between marker and record.

Hmm, but is it important enough? The tradeoff: tolerance (current) vs precision. The doc comment explicitly says "a marker mention inside a plain log line still returns null" — that claim is only true when no balanced JSON object with a `message` follows the mention. Slightly overstated doc. I'll file as SUGGESTION.

4. **`@visibleForTesting` on `balancedJsonObjectAfter`** — the function IS called from production code (`parseJsAppErrorLogLine`, same library). `visibleForTesting` means "do not reference from production code OUTSIDE this library"; in-library use is legal, no analyzer error (I verified: analyzer clean). But the annotation is semantically wrong — it tells readers/tools this is test-only surface, when it's actually a production helper that is additionally exported for tests. The file's own convention: `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` is public, no annotation, doc says "Exported for the engine's log tap and for tests". Consistent fix: drop the annotation (or keep the function private and test through parseJsAppErrorLogLine). Actually — testing `balancedJsonObjectAfter` directly isn't even done in the tests! The new tests only exercise `parseJsAppErrorLogLine`. So the annotation is doubly odd: it's not used by any test directly. Making it private (`_balancedJsonObjectAfter`) would be cleaner — no public API growth. SUGGESTION (API surface minimization). Actually, since it's used only within the library, private is strictly better: smaller public surface on a lib that `flutter_app` exports via `package:fa/apps/...`. Let me check whether the file is exported publicly.

Let me check how `js_app_error_channel.dart` is exported (package:fa).

5. **Missing test: unbalanced/truncated record under envelope.** The negative tests cover `not-json` (no `{` at all) and a record without message. But `balancedJsonObjectAfter` returning null for an UNBALANCED record (e.g. truncated line `[E] faAppError:{"kind":"showError","message":"x"` — truncated, no closing brace) → null. The function's doc says "Null when no balanced object exists" — there's no test for the truncated case (the exact failure mode named in the doc comment and the root cause: "a trailing envelope brace used to make the payload malformed JSON"). Wait, actually the truncated-record case: `[E] faAppError:{"kind":"showError","message":"x"` → indexOf finds `{`, scans to end without balance → null → parse returns null. A test for that would document the truncation contract. Minor test-coverage suggestion.

6. **The old-code behavior parity for a record followed by trailing content**: old `[E] faAppError:{json} trailing` → decode of `{json} trailing` fails → null. New → parses `{json}` → captured. This is the intended loosening. Fine.

7. **Error: what if the balanced object found is an ARRAY?** e.g. line `[E] faAppError:[{...}]` — indexOf('{') would find the object inside the array, decode → Map. Old code: decode of `[{...}]` → List, `decoded is Map<String,dynamic>` false → null. Edge case, not a wire shape. No regression concern (new behavior returns an event where old returned null — only if the JSON is an array wrapping a message-object; unrealistic).

8. **Performance**: O(n) single pass, `line[i]` on a String does code-unit access — fine for log lines.

9. **Dart string `r'\'`** — raw string containing one backslash. Correct.

### Engine integration — `_handleEngineLog`

Unchanged. `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` is also used... only in the engine log tap. OK.

### Test review

- The new group is pure Dart — runs on the PR gate. Good.
- Test 4 negative case: `'{id: [E] some plain log}'` — marker-free → null via indexOf. Good.
- `'{id: [E] faAppError:{"kind":"showError"}}'` — balanced object = `{"kind":"showError"}`, decodes, `fromLogJson` returns null (no message) → good, this documents that message-less decodes stay null.
- The test names/comments reproduce the transport explanation — helpful.

One test-design nit: test 1 "a plain structured record parses (the gh-1164 wire shape)" uses `'[E] faAppError:$record'` — includes the `[E] ` classification prefix. Goo…

3. 💡 SUGGESTION — missing negative test for the truncated/unbalanced record (the exact historical failure mode the doc calls "unbalanced — truncated record"), e.g. `parseJsAppErrorLogLine('[E] faAppError:{"kind":"showError","message":"x"')` → null. Cheap contract pin.

Any IMPORTANT/BLOCKING? Let me think hard about whether there's a real correctness issue.

- Does the fix risk double-capture or dedup-key changes? The event produced from the enveloped line has the same fields as from the plain line → same fingerprint → dedup gate unaffected. Fine.

- Does the parse change affect `peekLogs` or the raw `_onLog` path? No — `_onLog` still gets the raw line unchanged. Fine.

- Any case where the NEW parser returns null where OLD returned an event? Old required rest-of-line to be exactly valid JSON. If rest-of-line was exactly the record, new finds the same balanced span. Identical. The ONLY divergence: rest-of-line contained the record plus trailing junk — old null, new event (strictly more capturing). So no regression direction. 

- Is the balanced-scan confused by `//` or regex literals in the record? JSON has no comments or regex literals — string-awareness is complete for JSON. Fine.

- Unicode line separators (U+2028/U+2029) inside JSON strings: JSON.stringify escapes them? Actually JSON.stringify does NOT escape U+2028/U+2029 in older engines... but they'd still be inside a quoted string in the JSON text, so the scanner handles them (they're just chars). But could the TRANSPORT split the log line at a raw U+2028? If the runtime treats U+2028 as a line terminator when writing the log line, the record would split mid-string → unbalanced → null. This existed before equally (old parser would also fail on a split record). Not a regression.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1309
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1309
- **Title**: gh-1307 [BUG] nightly macOS suite red: js_app_error_capture_test — load error NOT captured (empty list) regression from #1273's engine fix, merged green through the PR exclusion-zone hole
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1307` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +93
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T09:06:45Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T10:57:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #1307
## Root Cause

- The gh-1164 error-capture surface was blind: `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` required the `faAppError:{json}` record to run to end-of-line, but by the time an engine log line reaches Dart it is wrapped in the runtime's iid-transport envelope — `{id: [E] faAppError:{…}}` (flutter_js `jsonDecode`s the `sendMessage` payload before the channel callback, so the bootstrap's `{"iid":…,"id":…}` wrap survives routing). The envelope's trailing brace made the payload malformed JSON → decode failed → `null` → the capture list stayed empty.
- #1273 (gh-1272) didn't break this path — it un-blinded it: before the raw-string bootstrap fix, no `faAppError` record was ever emitted (every widget dead); once records flowed again, the downstream parser mismatch surfaced. Green PR because the macOS flutter_app suite sits in the PR exclusion zone (#1267 N1 scenario, cross-linked).

## Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_error_channel.dart`: `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` now decodes the first **balanced** `{…}` object after the `faAppError:` marker (string-literal/escape-aware scan) instead of the exact rest-of-line — any transport envelope around the record decodes; plain-log marker mentions still return `null`. No change to the wire format, the bootstrap, #1272's raw-string fix, or the pinned `js_widget_runtime` package.

## Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_error_channel_test.dart`: 4 new pure-Dart parser tests (plain record, iid-enveloped record, nested braces/escapes, negative cases) — run everywhere, no JS bridge needed.
- `test/apps/js_app_error_capture_test.dart` (the red nightly suite): 3/3 PASSED with the native QuickJS bridge.
- Full `flutter_app/test/apps/` with the bridge: **528 passed, 0 failed** (incl. the gh-1272 regex round-trip group — AC2: corrupted/regex-heavy sources still eval, and load throws are captured with a readable `Widget error: …` message); engine suite 68 passed; agent_service error-delivery suite passed. Analyzer clean on touched files.

## Notes

- Load errors are reported with kind `showError` and message `Widget error: <reason>` (the runtime eval wrapper's text) — the gate/dedup/delivery semantics are unchanged.
- The runtime's `_routeMessage` string-unwrap branch is dead code on flutter_js backends (payloads arrive pre-decoded as Maps); left untouched here — the canonical parser now tolerates the envelope either way (NG2: one error surface).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
=====
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:

Now let me do the deep review of the actual change. Key analysis points so far:

### Correctness of `balancedJsonObjectAfter`

Let me trace through edge cases:

1. **Escape handling inside strings**: `\"` correctly skipped via `i++`. `\\` also. An escape at the very end (`i++` past length) → loop exits, returns null (unbalanced) — correct.

2. **Single quotes**: JSON strings are always double-quoted (JSON.stringify). But the ENVELOPE (`{id: [E] faAppError:...}`) is not JSON. The scan starts at the record's `{`, so envelope content doesn't matter. OK.

3. **The scan starts at the first `{` AFTER the marker** — so if a plain log line mentions the marker followed by text without `{`, returns null. If a log line contains `faAppError: {some other json}` that jsonDecodes to a Map with `message` — a false positive could capture a plain log as an error. That was equally possible in the old code (old code would also decode `{some other json}` if it were valid JSON with message field). No regression.

4. **Multiple `}` inside the record's strings** — handled by string-awareness.

5. **What if the record is valid but the envelope `}` trails** — handled (scan returns at record's balanced close).

6. **Behavior change for old wire shape**: `[E] faAppError:{json}` → old: substring to end = `{json}` → decode. New: balanced scan → `{json}`. Same. ✅ Backward compatible.

7. **Whitespace after marker**: old code `.trim()`ed the payload. New: `balancedJsonObjectAfter(line, index + marker.length)` — `indexOf('{', from)` skips leading whitespace. Equivalent. Trailing whitespace after record: old decode of `{json}  `.trim() would still work; new returns `{json}` — same. ✅

8. **Surrogate pairs**: no issue.

9. **`line[i]` performance**: For log lines this is O(n) — fine.

Now a REAL edge case worth thinking about: **a JSON string containing a backslash at end of string in the ENVELOPE** — not applicable since scan starts at record.

**A record that itself is not at the first `{` after marker**: e.g. line = `[E] faAppError: see {docs} then {"kind":"showError","message":"x"}`. New code picks `{docs}` → not balanced JSON (well `{docs}` IS balanced) → decode fails → null → capture misses. Old code: `see {docs} then {...}` → decode fails → null too. Same behavior (both miss). Not a regression, and not a real wire shape.

**The critical scenario the ticket cares about**: does the actual transport line contain the marker with the record AFTER it as the first `{`? Observed shape per PR/tests: `{id: [E] faAppError:{…}}` — yes, record's `{` is the first `{` after the marker. ✅

### Now the deeper question — NG2: "ONE canonical error surface"

The ticket's NG2 asks for one canonical error surface so a fix in one can't blind the other. This PR patches the parser tolerantly, but the ENGINE test (`js_app_error_capture_test.dart`) requires the real QuickJS bridge (skipped without it) — and the macOS suite is in the PR exclusion zone (the whole reason this regressed). apps library for a function with zero external users. No analyzer diagnostic
fires either way (in-library use is legal), so this is polish, not a bug.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the scan-to-first-`{` heuristic loosens capture precision more than the envelope fix requires**

`balancedJsonObjectAfter` jumps to the first `{` *anywhere* after the marker.
Combined with `fromLogJson`'s only real requirement (non-empty `message`), a
plain widget log line that merely *mentions* the marker and later contains any
balanced JSON object with a `message` string would now be captured as an agent-
facing error — the old rest-of-line contract rejected it:

```dart
// now captured (false positive):
widgetLog('the host parses faAppError: records like {"message":"hint"}');
```

The doc claim at line 42 ("a marker mention inside a plain log line still
returns null") holds only when no such JSON follows the mention. The blast
radius is small — the dedup gate + circuit breaker contain spurious reports,
and the bootstrap owns the marker today — but the fix can be made exact with
one guard: require the record's `{` to be the first non-whitespace character
after the marker. Both observed wire shapes already satisfy it:

- plain: `[E] faAppError:{json}` — immediate
- enveloped: `{id: [E] faAppError:{json}}` — immediate

so the gh-1307 fix stays intact while the heuristic narrows back to the record
itself. If you keep the looser scan, soften the line-42 doc claim instead.

💡 **SUGGESTION: pin the truncated-record contract with one more negative case**

`balancedJsonObjectAfter`'s own doc names the truncation exit ("Null when no
balanced object exists" — the loop ends with `depth > 0`), and a truncated
record is exactly the historical failure mode this parser class suffered
(payload cut mid-object → decode failed → capture stayed silent). None of the
four new tests exercises that path: `'[E] faAppError:not-json'` has no `{` at
all, and the other negatives fail in `fromLogJson`, not in the scanner.

One line pins the contract:

```dart
expect(
  parseJsAppErrorLogLine(
    '[E] faAppError:{"kind":"showError","message":"x"', // truncated — never closed
  ),
  isNull,
  reason: 'unbalanced record must stay null, not decode a prefix',
);
```

This also guards a subtle wrong-answer mode: if the scanner ever returned the
best-effort prefix instead of null, a truncated record could decode as a
different (shorter) object and produce a phantom event with a wrong
fingerprint, defeating the dedup gate.

## PR Description

Closes #1307
## Root Cause

- The gh-1164 error-capture surface was blind: `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` required the `faAppError:{json}` record to run to end-of-line, but by the time an engine log line reaches Dart it is wrapped in the runtime's iid-transport envelope — `{id: [E] faAppError:{…}}` (flutter_js `jsonDecode`s the `sendMessage` payload before the channel callback, so the bootstrap's `{"iid":…,"id":…}` wrap survives routing). The envelope's trailing brace made the payload malformed JSON → decode failed → `null` → the capture list stayed empty.
- #1273 (gh-1272) didn't break this path — it un-blinded it: before the raw-string bootstrap fix, no `faAppError` record was ever emitted (every widget dead); once records flowed again, the downstream parser mismatch surfaced. Green PR because the macOS flutter_app suite sits in the PR exclusion zone (#1267 N1 scenario, cross-linked).

## Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_error_channel.dart`: `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` now decodes the first **balanced** `{…}` object after the `faAppError:` marker (string-literal/escape-aware scan) instead of the exact rest-of-line — any transport envelope around the record decodes; plain-log marker mentions still return `null`. No change to the wire format, the bootstrap, #1272's raw-string fix, or the pinned `js_widget_runtime` package.

## Test Coverage

- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_error_channel_test.dart`: 4 new pure-Dart parser tests (plain record, iid-enveloped record, nested braces/escapes, negative cases) — run everywhere, no JS bridge needed.
- `test/apps/js_app_error_capture_test.dart` (the red nightly suite): 3/3 PASSED with the native QuickJS bridge.
- Full `flutter_app/test/apps/` with the bridge: **528 passed, 0 failed** (incl. the gh-1272 regex round-trip group — AC2: corrupted/regex-heavy sources still eval, and load throws are captured with a readable `Widget error: …` message); engine suite 68 passed; agent_service error-delivery suite passed. Analyzer clean on touched files.

## Notes

- Load errors are reported with kind `showError` and message `Widget error: <reason>` (the runtime eval wrapper's text) — the gate/dedup/delivery semantics are unchanged.
- The runtime's `_routeMessage` string-unwrap branch is dead code on flutter_js backends (payloads arrive pre-decoded as Maps); left untouched here — the canonical parser now tolerates the envelope either way (NG2: one error surface).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
=====
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
  `package-lock.json`s, and `vendor/wasm_run/native/Cargo.lock`); a listed
  lockfile that is missing/untracked/gitignored fails the Static gates, and
  pod-sync (flutter-analyze + nightly build legs, after `pub get`) fails
  when a native iOS/macOS plugin resolved by pubspec.lock has no pod in the
  platform's `Podfile.lock` (the gh-1274 class), or its pod is pinned at a
  stale version vs the resolved plugin podspec's `s.version` (the
  flutter_gemma 1.8.0-vs-1.11.3 skew; the podspec is the comparison target,
  not the pubspec version — vendored/beta pods legitimately differ from the
  Dart package version). After ANY pubspec.yaml
  dependency change that adds/updates a darwin-native plugin: `cd
  flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update` and the same in `macos/`,
  commit both `Podfile.lock`s (CocoaPods runs fine on Linux for
  regeneration; the wasm_run `nm` step needs an llvm-nm shim + the
  XCFramework staged via `scripts/setup_vendor_ios.sh` or the upstream zip).
  Guard red exits are fixture-self-tested (`scripts/
  check_lockfiles_selftest.sh`, Static gates).
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly

  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the le…

### Correctness of `balancedJsonObjectAfter`

Let me trace through edge cases:

1. **Escape handling inside strings**: `\"` correctly skipped via `i++`. `\\` also. An escape at the very end (`i++` past length) → loop exits, returns null (unbalanced) — correct.

2. **Single quotes**: JSON strings are always double-quoted (JSON.stringify). But the ENVELOPE (`{id: [E] faAppError:...}`) is not JSON. The scan starts at the record's `{`, so envelope content doesn't matter. OK.

3. **The scan starts at the first `{` AFTER the marker** — so if a plain log line mentions the marker followed by text without `{`, returns null. If a log line contains `faAppError: {some other json}` that jsonDecodes to a Map with `message` — a false positive could capture a plain log as an error. That was equally possible in the old code (old code would also decode `{some other json}` if it were valid JSON with message field). No regression.

4. **Multiple `}` inside the record's strings** — handled by string-awareness.

5. **What if the record is valid but the envelope `}` trails** — handled (scan returns at record's balanced close).

7. **Whitespace after marker**: old code `.trim()`ed the payload. New: `balancedJsonObjectAfter(line, index + marker.length)` — `indexOf('{', from)` skips leading whitespace. Equivalent. Trailing whitespace after record: old decode of `{json}  `.trim() would still work; new returns `{json}` — same. ✅

8. **Surrogate pairs**: no issue.

9. **`line[i]` performance**: For log lines this is O(n) — fine.

Now a REAL edge case worth thinking about: **a JSON string containing a backslash at end of string in the ENVELOPE** — not applicable since scan starts at record.

**A record that itself is not at the first `{` after marker**: e.g. line = `[E] faAppError: see {docs} then {"kind":"showError","message":"x"}`. New code picks `{docs}` → not balanced JSON (well `{docs}` IS balanced) → decode fails → null → capture misses. Old code: `see {docs} then {...}` → decode fails → null too. Same behavior (both miss). Not a regression, and not a real wire shape.

**The critical scenario the ticket cares about**: does the actual transport line contain the marker with the record AFTER it as the first `{`? Observed shape per PR/tests: `{id: [E] faAppError:{…}}` — yes, record's `{` is the first `{` after the marker. ✅
